rules.title: Python cannot import a module
rules.summary: The active interpreter cannot find the requested module on sys.path.
causes: The dependency is not installed in the active environment.
pip and python point to different interpreters.
The import name differs from the package name.
actions: Check which python executable is running and whether its virtual environment is active.
Use that interpreter's python -m pip to inspect installed packages.

rules.title: Python marked this environment as externally managed
rules.summary: The operating system owns this Python installation and blocks global pip changes.
causes: The distribution protects system Python packages from pip.
The command is running outside a virtual environment.
actions: Create and activate a virtual environment for the project.
Use the operating system package manager only for system-wide packages.
Avoid --break-system-packages unless you fully own the environment.

rules.title: pip found no compatible distribution
rules.summary: The index has no release matching the requested version and current platform constraints.

any: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement

causes: The package name or version is wrong.
No wheel supports the current Python, operating system, or CPU.
The configured package index does not contain the release.
actions: Confirm the package name and available versions on the configured index.
Check the active Python version and platform tags.
Inspect proxy or private-index configuration if a known release is missing.

rules.title: The package does not support this Python version
rules.summary: Package metadata excludes the active Python interpreter.

any: Ignored the following versions that require a different python version

causes: The project is using an older or newer Python than the package supports.
A resolver selected a release with incompatible Requires-Python metadata.
actions: Compare python --version with the project's requires-python declaration.
Use a supported interpreter or select a compatible package release.

rules.title: Python cannot create a virtual environment
rules.summary: The interpreter was installed without the ensurepip or venv components.
causes: The operating system splits venv support into a separate package.
This Python build intentionally omitted ensurepip.
actions: Install the venv component that matches the exact Python version using the operating system's package manager.
Recreate the virtual environment after the component is installed.
